members.name: range_expansion_breakout_v1
members.thesis: When a stock trades in a tight intraday base (range < 0.3% over 30+ bars), it represents a balance between supply and demand at a specific price level. When this base 'expands' — a single bar has a range > 3x the average bar range of the base period — it signals that the equilibrium has broken. The
entry_long: expansion_ratio > 3.0 (current bar range is 3x the base average)
members.exit_target: base_range projected from breakout level (measured move = base height from breakout point)
members.exit_stop: opposite side of the base (if long, stop at base low; if short, stop at base high)
filters: India_VIX < 22; tight bases are more meaningful in moderate vol
no entries before 10:00 (need 30+ bars of data) or after 14:30
prefer expansions in direction of VWAP and NIFTY 50 trend
weaknesses: Tight bases are rare intraday — may see 0-1 qualifying setups per day across the universe
The 3x expansion ratio can be triggered by a single anomalous bar (news flash, fat finger) — not always genuine momentum
Using base range as the target may be too ambitious if the base is very tight (0.1% base = 0.1% target, below costs)

members.name: consolidation_breakout_v1
members.thesis: A mid-session consolidation occurs when price trades in a range < 0.2% for 20+ consecutive bars after an initial directional move. This pattern represents institutional order absorption: large limit orders create a ceiling/floor, absorbing aggressive orders until the limit order is fully filled. Whe
entry_long: prior_move_dir > 0 (consolidation after an up-move = bullish continuation pattern)
entry_short: prior_move_dir < 0 (consolidation after a down-move = bearish continuation pattern)
members.exit_target: magnitude of the prior move projected from consolidation (measured move)
members.exit_stop: opposite side of consolidation range (consol_low for longs, consol_high for shorts)
filters: breakout bar volume > 2x consolidation average volume
continuation bias: long if prior move was up, short if prior move was down
weaknesses: Consolidation patterns can break in either direction; the prior_move_dir filter helps but continuation is not guaranteed
Very tight consolidation (0.2%) may be below the noise floor of some stocks — what looks like consolidation may be normal low-vol drift
Measured move targeting assumes symmetry (move after = move before consolidation) which is often not the case in practice
members.prior_art: Flag and pennant patterns are the classic continuation patterns (Edwards & Magee). The tight consolidation breakout is essentially a flag pattern quantified. Bulkowski's 'Encyclopedia of Chart Pattern
